name: Peoples of California
summary: The many Indigenous peoples of California, such as the Chumash, Pomo, Miwok, Yurok and Yokuts, among the most densely settled foragers in the world; about 300,000 people speaking some 90 languages lived there before Spanish missions (from 1769) and the Gold Rush (1849) devastated them.

knownFor.label: Pomo baskets
knownFor.note: Some of the finest baskets in the world.

knownFor.label: Acorn food
knownFor.note: Acorns leached and ground into meal.

location.value: Traditional homelands may not match California’s boundaries; some groups lived on the Nevada, Oregon and Baja California borders.
location.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of California (checked 12 Nov 2026)

terrain.value: A varied land of coast, valleys, mountains and deserts.

climate.value: Mediterranean on the coast; dry in the south-east.

resources.value: Acorns, salmon, shellfish, deer and seeds, which supported dense populations.

disasters.value: Mission-era disease and the Gold Rush; 100,000 Native people are said to have died in the gold rush’s first two years (discovery at Sutter’s Mill, 1848).
disasters.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of California (checked 12 Nov 2026)

population.value: About 340,000 at the first mission in 1769 (possibly more); about 30,000 by 1870 (other article figures vary).
population.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of California (checked 12 Nov 2026)

urbanisation.value: Sub-tribes of 50 to 500 members; villages of 400 to 500 people.
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of California (checked 12 Nov 2026)

disease.value: Disease, crowding and mission conditions after 1769; missions recorded 63,789 deaths from 1769 to 1832; a malaria epidemic in 1833.
disease.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of California (checked 12 Nov 2026)

migration.value: Very stable; some groups lived in the same area for thousands of years.

economicBase.value: Acorns (a primary food), salmon and shellfish; land kept open by controlled burning.
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of California (checked 12 Nov 2026)

tradeRoutes.value: Trade networks across California; shell-bead money.

wealth.value: Shell beads and obsidian were valued as wealth.

inequality.value: Mostly small-scale societies; some ranked chiefs and families.

governmentType.value: Independent villages and “tribelets” led by chiefs.

keyRulers.value: Village chiefs; few names are recorded before contact.

succession.value: Chiefs were often hereditary, though skill and generosity mattered.

eliteConflict.value: Local disputes, usually settled within or between villages.

armyAndTech.value: Bows and arrows, and fine basketry.

majorWars.value: The article calls the conflicts from about 1846 to 1873 the California genocide.
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of California (checked 12 Nov 2026)

territoryChange.value: Eighteen treaties of 1851 guaranteed about 7.5 million acres (about one-seventh of California); they were shelved and never ratified.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of California (checked 12 Nov 2026)

alliancesRivals.value: Neighbouring peoples traded and sometimes fought.

inventions.value: No major inventions are recorded; skilled local technologies.

scienceEducation.value: Oral knowledge of plants, stars and land management.

communicationTransport.value: Trails and plank or tule-reed boats, such as the Chumash tomol.

religion.value: Kuksu religion, practised by many tribes in central and northern California (Nisenan, Maidu, Pomo, Patwin).
religion.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of California (checked 12 Nov 2026)

languageWriting.value: At least 78 languages in the 1769 context; about 100 by another count (over 300 dialects).
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of California (checked 12 Nov 2026)

artsArchitecture.value: Chumash rock art (pictographs) in southern California.
artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of California (checked 12 Nov 2026)

socialStructure.value: Families and lineages in small polities.

sharedIdentity.value: Identity rested on each people, village and language rather than one state.

dailyLife.value: Acorns ground into meal and leached of tannins; salmon was the defining food for the Yurok and Karuk.
dailyLife.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of California (checked 12 Nov 2026)

neighbours.value: Great Basin and Southwest peoples; Spanish missions.

ideasReligions.value: Land was carefully managed by fire and tended in a spiritual way.

colonisation.value: Long-term Spanish occupation from 1769 (Mission San Diego de Alcalá); coastal tribes met European explorers in the mid-16th century.
colonisation.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of California (checked 12 Nov 2026)

riseSignals.value: Thousands of years of settlement and resource management.

peakPeriod.value: The period before Spanish missions began in 1769.

declineSignals.value: The mission system (from 1769) and the Gold Rush (discovery 1848).
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of California (checked 12 Nov 2026)

outcome.value: Many of these peoples survive today, some with their own governments.

overallCertainty.value: Known from archaeology, oral history and Spanish and later records; population figures are estimates.
